name: todo-txt
description: Edits a todo.txt file: one task per line, no database. Point it at a folder you already sync, or use the one it creates. Priorities, projects, contexts and due dates colour as you type, and the format's semantics actually run rather than just highlight: rec: rollover on completion, t: thresholds, h:1 hidden tasks. Palette verbs match the todo.txt CLI. Archiving moves completed tasks to done.txt. AI rewrites the lines you select, and stages any deletion as a diff you approve.
author: LeTeutz
highlights: Reads and writes a todo.txt in any folder, including one your sync tool already watches. The path is stored in the app's settings.json.
Saves 400ms after you stop typing, or straight away once four seconds of unbroken typing have passed.
If the file changed on disk, the save is refused and your text stays in the editor. Nothing is merged and nothing is discarded.
A 5-second poll watches for edits made elsewhere. It reloads a buffer with no unsaved work, and asks first when you have some.
An interrupted session reopens as a recovery draft you accept or discard.
Multi-cursor, coloured priorities, Tab-completion for +projects and @contexts, and an optional VIM mode with todo.txt leader keys.
Palette verbs match the todo.txt CLI: add, do, pri, depri, sort, deduplicate, archive, move, listproj, report.
filter @work pri:A-C due:<=7d dims the non-matching lines. The file is untouched. An option hides t: and h:1 tasks.
rec:1w schedules from the day you complete a task; rec:+1w schedules from its due: date. Monthly and yearly steps clamp to real month ends.
An additive AI rewrite applies after a snapshot. One that deletes a line is staged as a diff until you approve it.
done.txt is a tab of its own with rotating backups. report.txt is append-only, drawn as a 90-day active-versus-done chart.
